l-honorable-rene-edouard-caron

A dignified man in dark formal clothes sits for his portrait. René-Édouard Caron was a mayor of Quebec City and later a lieutenant-governor. Théophile Hamel was one of Quebec's most important portrait painters, trained in Europe in the 1840s. It's a typical example of the serious portraits that recorded the leaders of early Canada.
l-abbe-patrick-mcmahon

A priest in a black robe and white collar looks out with a calm, thoughtful face. Théophile Hamel painted many portraits of religious and political leaders in Quebec. His portraits are known for their lifelike faces and clear lines. It's a good example of Canadian portraiture in the 1840s.
jeunes-indiennes-a-lorette

Two young Indigenous girls from Wendake (then called Lorette), a Huron-Wendat village near Quebec City, pose in their dresses. Théophile Hamel painted them with great sympathy and care. Many Quebec artists visited Wendake to paint portraits. It's a gentle record of the people who lived there.
study-for-northern-river

Tom Thomson made this quick sketch for a larger painting of a river in northern Ontario, with rocks and trees in bold color. Thomson was a Canadian painter who spent summers canoeing in Algonquin Park, painting small oil sketches on wooden panels. His fresh, colorful style inspired the Group of Seven. It's a peek at how he began a painting.
northern-river

A river runs through the northern Ontario wilderness, with dark evergreens and a sky glowing orange and pink at sunset. Tom Thomson painted this in 1915, and it is one of his most famous pictures. It was bought by the Canadian government and hangs in the National Gallery of Canada. It's a classic image of the Canadian north.
in-the-northland

Wind-bent trees and rocks stand on the shore of a bright lake, in strong, warm colors. Tom Thomson painted this wild landscape in Algonquin Park. The bold color and thick paint show his modern style. It was one of the paintings that helped make him a Canadian legend.
canadian-wildflowers

A small bouquet of wildflowers bursts with orange, yellow and blue against a dark background. Tom Thomson is best known for landscapes, but he also painted flowers as small sketches. The glowing colors have a joyful energy. It's a rare and cheerful still life.
autumn-s-garland

Bright red and orange autumn leaves stand out against the dark woods, painted on a small panel. Tom Thomson loved the Ontario fall, when the maples blaze with color. His small sketches captured the feeling of the season. It's a vivid example of Canadian autumn.
burnt-land

Charred tree trunks stand on a hill after a forest fire, with new green growth rising beneath them. Tom Thomson saw the burnt land in Algonquin Park and made it the subject of a powerful sketch. Despite the damage, the spring colors show hope. It's a famous image of nature recovering.
blue-lake-sketch-for-in-the-northland

A deep blue lake is surrounded by bright trees in a quick, colorful study. Tom Thomson made it as a first idea for his painting 'In the Northland.' The sketch is full of fresh, direct feeling. It shows how he worked outdoors, painting fast.
the-jack-pine

A twisted pine tree stands alone on a rocky shore, with a glowing lake and a sunset sky behind it. Tom Thomson painted this in 1916, and it became one of the most famous paintings in Canada. The lonely tree stands for strength in the wild northern land. It hangs in the National Gallery of Canada in Ottawa.
spring-ice

Pale blue ice melts on a lake in spring, with dark trees and a golden sky. Tom Thomson painted the thawing lake in Algonquin Park. The painting is an early sign of spring in the north. It's one of his finest winter-to-spring scenes.
sketch-for-the-west-wind

A wind-bent pine and a rough lake are painted quickly on a small panel. Tom Thomson made this sketch as a first draft for his masterpiece, 'The West Wind.' You can see how he worked out the wind and the waves. It's a rare look at the first idea for a great painting.
boats

Boats rest by the shore of a lake in dappled light. Tom Thomson often painted on Canoe Lake in Algonquin Park, where he lived and worked as a guide. The little sketch is relaxed and bright. It's a happy picture of life on the water.
the-west-wind

A twisted pine bends in a strong wind, with whitecaps on the lake and clouds streaming across a blue and gold sky. Tom Thomson painted this in the winter of 1916–17, and it is one of the most beloved paintings in Canada. He drowned mysteriously in a lake in 1917, shortly afterward, which made him a legend. The painting hangs in the Art Gallery of Ontario.
the-phantom-hunter

A ghostly hunter and his dog lead a pack of spectral figures across a snowy field in a haunting night scene. William Blair Bruce, a Canadian painter from Hamilton, Ontario, painted this in France. It tells an old folk tale about a ghostly hunt. It's a dramatic, spooky picture.
behind-bonsecours-market-montreal

A quiet corner of old Montreal sits behind Bonsecours Market, with houses, snow and carts. William Raphael, born in Prussia, settled in Montreal and painted its streets and markets. His pictures record the look of the city in the 1860s. It's a historic snapshot of Montreal.
zacharie-vincent-et-son-fils-cyprien

Zacharie Vincent, a Huron-Wendat artist, painted himself and his son, dressed in traditional clothing. He is considered the first Indigenous painter in Quebec, and he signed his work 'the last of the Hurons.' It is a proud self-portrait that shows both identity and strength. It's an important work in Canadian art history.
portrait-of-a-young-man

A young man with an earnest face looks out of the frame. Adolph Tidemand, a Norwegian painter who lived in Düsseldorf, Germany, painted portraits as well as scenes of Norwegian farm life. He helped create the image of Norway's peasants as national heroes. It's an early portrait from his career.
study-of-a-horse

A study of a horse in strong, lively lines. Adolph Tidemand made drawings and paintings of animals as practice for his big pictures of Norwegian life. The horse is full of character. It's a lovely small study.
low-church-devotion

Farmers and families in traditional costumes gather for a prayer meeting in a simple farmhouse, with plain wooden walls. Adolph Tidemand painted this scene of a Hauge movement gathering, a popular Norwegian religious revival. It's famous for its honest look at Norwegian country life. The picture has become a symbol of Norwegian folk culture.
low-church-devotion-1852

Another version of Tidemand's scene of a farmhouse prayer gathering, with a dim room, simple clothing and serious faces. Tidemand painted several versions because the first was so popular. The soft light on the faces and the quiet atmosphere are moving. It's a picture of faith in Norwegian rural life.
the-return-of-the-bear-hunter

A hunter returns home with a bear he's killed, as the family and villagers greet him. Adolph Tidemand painted scenes of Norwegian rural life that were popular across Europe. The hunter is a hero. It's a scene from a harsh but proud way of life.
kunstnerviften

A group of artists, women and men, gather in friendly conversation. Asta Nørregaard, one of Norway's first professional women painters, painted her colleagues in Kristiania (now Oslo). It records the lively art community of the 1890s. It's a picture of friendship among artists.
after-first-communion

A family sits together at home after a church ceremony, in their best clothes. Carl Frithjof Smith, a Norwegian painter who lived in Germany, painted quiet scenes of family life. The mood is peaceful and warm. It's a gentle picture of a special day.
portrait-of-the-swedish-painter-karl-nordstrom

A man with a strong, thoughtful face looks out of a dark background. Christian Krohg, a Norwegian painter, painted his friend Karl Nordström, a Swedish artist. The two met in the artists' colony in Grez-sur-Loing near Paris. It's a portrait of friendship between Nordic artists.
mother-and-child

A mother tenderly holds her baby close in a quiet room. Christian Krohg, a Norwegian painter and writer, often painted mothers and the lives of ordinary women. The soft light shows the love between them. It's a gentle, warm picture.
portrait-of-jossa

A woman looks out with a calm, direct gaze in a warm, simple style. Christian Krohg painted his models and friends honestly, in the Realist tradition. He was a leading painter in Norway's art world. It's a lively portrait.
braiding-her-hair
A young woman sits and braids her long hair, lost in thought. Christian Krohg painted private, quiet moments with a Realist eye. The soft light and calm are charming. It's a peaceful scene.
portrait-of-the-painter-oda-krohg-b-lasson

A woman with an elegant look sits in a chair, with her hands in her lap. Oda Krohg was a painter herself and Christian Krohg's wife, and an important figure in the Kristiania art world. Her husband painted her several times. It's a tribute from one artist to another.
struggle-for-survival

A long line of poor people stand in the cold outside a charity office, waiting for help in the snow. Christian Krohg painted this in 1889 to draw attention to poverty in Kristiania (Oslo). He wanted his art to make people care. It's one of the most important Norwegian paintings about social issues.
leiv-eirikson-discovering-america

The Viking explorer Leif Erikson stands in the bow of a longship, gazing at the shore of a new land, with his crew behind him. Christian Krohg painted this in 1893 for the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, which celebrated Columbus. Norwegians wanted to remind everyone that Vikings reached North America around the year 1000. It's a proud picture of Viking history.
night-in-saint-cloud

A man sits in a dark room by a window, with the blue of a night glowing behind him. Edvard Munch painted it in 1890, at a time when he was living in France and mourning his father. The strong blue shapes make a quiet, lonely feeling. It's an early work that shows the mood of his later art.
kiss-by-the-window

A couple embraces in front of a window, with the curtain and the dark shapes nearby. Edvard Munch painted several pictures of kisses, which were among his favorite subjects. The shapes of the two people almost melt together. It's a very personal and quiet moment.
self-portrait-with-cigarette

Munch stands in the shadows, with smoke curling from his cigarette, looking out at the viewer. He painted many self-portraits during his long life, because they were a way to study his own feelings. The dark and smoky colors give a moody look. It's a well-known Norwegian portrait.
separation

A man stands at a seashore while a woman with long hair seems to melt away, with her hair flowing in the wind. Edvard Munch painted about the pain of parting. The colors of sea and sky are quiet, but the mood is sad. It's one of his emotional pictures of love and loss.
friedrich-nietzsche

The famous German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche is painted in a strong, bold style. Edvard Munch made this portrait in 1906 for a Swedish collector, even though Nietzsche had died in 1900, so he painted him from a photograph and from memory. The expressive lines seem to show an intense thinker. It's a portrait of an idea as much as a man.
nocturne

A quiet blue night scene with the moon and shimmering water, with few figures. Eilif Peterssen was a Norwegian painter who liked painting history, portraits and mood. Many Norwegian painters in the 1880s painted this kind of atmospheric night. It's a calm and dreamy picture.
helvig-paus
A woman sits in a calm pose, with her hands folded. Eilif Peterssen painted many portraits of leading Norwegians. This one comes from late in his career. It's a dignified and graceful portrait.
peasant-burial

Villagers carry a coffin through a snowy countryside, with mourners following in a long line. Erik Werenskiold, a Norwegian painter, painted this to show real Norwegian farm life without prettiness. It was celebrated as one of the first truly Norwegian paintings. It's a serious, moving picture.
karen-inga-basker-werenskiold

A woman looks thoughtfully out of a warm, quiet portrait. Erik Werenskiold painted his family and close friends with honesty. He was one of the most respected Norwegian painters, and also illustrated Norwegian fairy tales. It's an affectionate family portrait.
winter-evening

A snowy landscape lit by a pink and gold evening sky, with blue shadows on the snow. Fredrik Borgen was a Norwegian painter who painted the quiet moods of winter. The painting makes the cold feel gentle and calm. It's a beautiful winter view.
winter-in-norway

A small stream runs through a snowy landscape, with the blue and white of winter. Frits Thaulow was a Norwegian painter who loved to paint water, in rivers and streams, often in winter. He painted with a pure and clear touch. It's a lovely view of a Norwegian winter.
from-vaterfjord

A quiet fjord scene with calm water and mountains in the background. Gunnar Berg was a Norwegian painter who painted the landscapes of northern Norway. The calm water is like a mirror. It's a peaceful picture.
breakfast-i-the-artist-s-mother-and-brother

A mother and son sit at a simple breakfast table in a warm, bright room. Gustav Wentzel painted this scene of his own family, in a very honest and everyday way. Many Norwegian painters of the 1880s wanted to show real life as it was. It's a cozy and truthful picture.
evening-of-summer

A calm Norwegian summer evening, with a soft glow in the sky and the stillness of the land. Halfdan Egedius was a young Norwegian painter who died at only 25, but who painted with great sensitivity. The quiet mood is almost like music. It's a gentle and dreamy landscape.
ndhavn-ved-norskekysten

A ship finds shelter from a storm at a safe harbor on the Norwegian coast, with a sky of clouds. Hans Gude, a leading Norwegian painter, was a master of ships and the sea. He taught many younger painters in Germany. It's a dramatic coast picture.
the-sandvik-fiord

Mountains rise over a calm fjord, with the water reflecting the sky and a few boats. Hans Gude painted the grand scenery of Norway, which made him one of the most famous Norwegian painters. The picture shows the beauty of the fjords. It's a classic Norwegian view.
at-the-window

A woman sits near a window, reading in the soft light. Hans Heyerdahl was a Norwegian painter who painted quiet indoor scenes and portraits. The gentle light shows his skill. It's a peaceful moment at home.
ulysses-s-grant

A general with a beard and a serious look stands in uniform. Ulysses S. Grant led the Union army in the American Civil War and later became the 18th president of the United States. This portrait was painted by Ole Peter Hansen Balling, a Norwegian-born painter who fought in the Civil War himself. It's a link between Norway and American history.
chester-a-arthur

The 21st president of the United States, Chester A. Arthur, sits for a formal portrait with a calm, serious expression. Ole Peter Hansen Balling was a Norwegian-born painter who moved to America and painted famous Americans. His portraits tell us how both countries are connected. It's an interesting piece of Norwegian-American art.
blue-interior

A woman sits in a dim room, with deep blue shadows and soft, warm light. Harriet Backer was one of Norway's most important painters, and was famous for painting the glow of light inside a room. She taught many younger artists. It's one of the most beautiful pictures of indoor light in Norwegian art.
